title: Groupoid laws on presheaves and the canonical algebraic-space stabilizer
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $U,R$ be presheaves of sets on schemes over $S$, in the universes of [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Given natural transformations $s,t:R\to U$, $e:U\to R$, $i:R\to R$ and $c:R\times_{s,U,t}R\to R$ (fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product]), the groupoid-law predicate means that on every test scheme $T/S$ these maps give a groupoid with objects $U(T)$, arrows $R(T)$, source $s$, target $t$, identities $e$, inverses $i$, and composition $c(a,b)=a\circ b$. Explicitly, $se=te=1$, $si=t$, $ti=s$, the source of $c(a,b)$ is $s(b)$ and its target is $t(a)$, the two identity and two inverse laws hold, and composition is associative. Naturality in $T$ is supplied by the natural transformations. Define its stabilizer presheaf to be the canonical pullback $U\times_{\Delta,U\times U,(s,t)}R$, with $\Delta=(1,1)$. When $U$ and $R$ are underlying presheaves of algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], this is their usual groupoid and stabilizer construction.

source.place: definition-groupoid and its following paragraph; definition-stabilizer-groupoid, with B=S. The same pointwise formulas extend to presheaves.
